comparison.objective: Candidate separates ceramic media from steel washers; pr-1891 seats an add-on PCB onto two rows of header pins without bending them.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests bimanual load sharing and orientation-sensitive sifting through many apertures; pr-1891 tests fine angular alignment and even force-controlled insertion of a tilted board onto pins. Both demand controlled orientation, but the contact mechanics and manipulation goal differ.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate grades recovery fraction, washer retention, support replacement, release, and spill/damage history; pr-1891 grades leveling, insertion depth, absence of pin bending, full seating, release, and a 1 s hold. No material rubric detail is missing.
comparison.reason: Selective many-body separation is not equivalent to tolerance-sensitive rigid-part alignment and press-fit insertion.
